title: Marked-anodyne restriction of Cartesian join slices
statement:
Use simplicial sets, standard simplices, degreewise pullbacks from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], inner fibrations and horn-Cartesian edges from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], marked simplicial sets and marked-anodyne maps from [lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus], and trivial Kan fibrations from [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration]. For simplicial sets $X,Y$, the ordered join has $(X\star Y)_n=X_n\amalg Y_n\amalg\coprod_{a+b+1=n}X_a\times Y_b$, with operators restricting the ordered $X$-block followed by the $Y$-block. Work in any one containing universe. Let $p:E\to B$ be an inner fibration of quasicategories. Let $i:U\hookrightarrow V$ be a marked-anodyne map of marked simplicial sets, and let $q:V\to E$ be a simplicial map carrying every marked edge of $V$ to a $p$-Cartesian edge. Put $q_0=qi$. For any simplicial diagram $a:L\to E$, define the ordered join slice by
$$(E_{/a})_n=\{\sigma:\Delta^n\star L\to E\mid \sigma|_L=a\},$$
with operators given by precomposition with $\Delta(\alpha)\star\operatorname{id}_L$; define $B_{/pa}$ in the same way. Then the simplicial restriction map
$$E_{/q}\longrightarrow E_{/q_0}\times_{B_{/pq_0}}B_{/pq},\qquad \sigma\longmapsto(\sigma|_{\Delta^n\star U},p\sigma),$$
is a trivial Kan fibration. In particular it lifts every simplicial boundary inclusion, including dimension zero, with exact agreement over the displayed target. No existence of Cartesian lifts other than the specified marked images is assumed, and no cardinal bound relative to a smaller universe is placed on $E,B,U,V$.

source.place: Higher Topos Theory, Proposition 3.1.1.11, printed p.151 (PDF page 169), with ordered join slices and the horn criterion of Proposition 2.4.1.8. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived under literature/. No Stacks tag states this marked quasicategorical result.

proof.text: Fix n≥0 and a boundary lifting square for the displayed restriction map. By the definitions of the ordered join slices and of degreewise pullback, its data are exactly a simplicial map h from J_n=((∂Δ[n]⋆V)∪_{∂Δ[n]⋆U}(Δ[n]⋆U)) to E, a map β:Δ[n]⋆V→B, and the equality ph=β|_{J_n}; h restricts to q on the V-part of ∂Δ[n]⋆V and β restricts to pq on V. An extension σ:Δ[n]⋆V→E with σ|_{Δ[n]⋆U} equal to the prescribed E-slice simplex and pσ=β is precisely a diagonal for this square. The formula also covers n=0 because ∂Δ[0] is empty.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.11, reduction of the boundary lifting problem to the ordered-join pushout

proof.text: Check the four generator families in [lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus] directly. For U=Λ_i^k and V=Δ^k, concatenate the n+1 initial vertices with the k+1 final vertices to identify Δ[n]⋆Δ[k] with Δ[n+k+1]. Under this identification J_n is Λ_{n+1+i}^{n+k+1}: its first summand contains precisely the faces omitting an initial vertex, and its second contains the faces omitting a final vertex other than n+1+i. This also proves the equality on all simplices, since membership in each of these simplicial subsets is determined by the image of its vertex map. For family (i), 0<i<k, hence 0<n+1+i<n+k+1, and the inner-fibration property of p gives the filler. For family (ii), i=k and k≥1, so this is the final horn of dimension n+k+1≥2. Its final edge lies in the prescribed V-part and is q applied to the marked final edge of Δ[k]; the defining p-Cartesian horn condition therefore gives the filler. This includes k=1, even though that edge is absent from the original horn U. Families (iii) and (iv) are identities on underlying simplicial sets. For either, J_n→Δ[n]⋆V is consequently an isomorphism, so h itself gives the required underlying simplicial filler; there is no marking to extend in E. These computations use the ordered join, not the Cartesian-product pushout product.

source.place: Definition 3.1.1.1, families (1)-(4), and Proposition 3.1.1.11, printed p.151 (PDF page 169): explicit ordered-join horn calculation, with the Cartesian outer-horn condition of def-coef-infinity-fibrations.

proof.text: The preceding cell argument is stable under the closure operations defining marked-anodyne maps. A pushout stage is solved by composing the already constructed diagonal with the pushout universal property; at a transfinite stage, the compatible diagonals on earlier stages assemble because simplicial sets and their marked-edge subsets are degreewise colimits; and a retract stage is solved by inserting the retract and projection maps. Therefore every map J_n→E over β extends to Δ[n]⋆V→E, with the extension agreeing on Δ[n]⋆U and projecting exactly to β. This proves the required boundary lifting for every n≥1 and the vertex-surjectivity case n=0.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.11, closure of the marked-anodyne cell argument

proof.text: By the definition of trivial Kan fibration, surjectivity on 0-simplices together with the boundary fillers for every n≥1 is exactly the assertion that E_{/q}→E_{/q_0}×_{B_{/pq_0}}B_{/pq} is a trivial Kan fibration. Since every diagonal was constructed over the prescribed β and relative to the prescribed Δ[n]⋆U-map, the restriction and base-projection equalities are strict, giving the stated exact agreement and the dimension-zero lifting assertion.

split_report.summary: The unchanged relative ordered-join slice statement is proved by translating boundary lifting into J_n, computing J_n explicitly as a single shifted horn for generator families (i) and (ii), observing that families (iii) and (iv) are underlying identities, extending the lifting property under pushouts, transfinite compositions and retracts, and applying the explicit trivial-Kan definition including n=0. No Cartesian-product-to-join comparison is used, and no new nodes are needed.
